title: Division 7A — payments, loans and forgiven debts treated as dividends
summary: Division 7A treats certain payments, loans and forgiven debts by a private company to a shareholder or associate as unfrankable dividends unless an exception applies. The flowchart covers the trigger provisions (ss 109C, 109D, 109F), interposed entity tracing (ss 109T-109U), the shareholder/associate nexus, the s 109C(3) payment definition and carve-outs, the payment-converted-to-loan reclassification (s 109D(4A)), the loan-repaid-before-lodgment day carve-out (s 109D(1)(b)), the s 109F(3)-(8) forgiveness rules, the s 109G debt-forgiveness exceptions, the Subdivision D exceptions (ss 109J-109NA) as individual decision nodes, amalgamated loans (s 109E), the distributable surplus cap (s 109Y), franking and character consequences (ss 109Z-109ZB), trust UPE limb (s 109XA), Commissioner discretion (s 109RB), and family law franking (s 109RC). Subsection coverage: ss 109C-109ZE mapped to nodes.

nodes.label: A private company makes a payment, loan, or forgives a debt to an entity
nodes.body: Division 7A may treat the amount as an unfrankable dividend if the entity is a shareholder or associate and no exception applies. The three triggers are: payment to an entity (s 109C), loan to an entity (s 109D), and forgiveness of all or part of a debt owed to the company (s 109F). Payment includes the provision of an asset for use (s 109CA).

nodes.label: What type of dealing with the private company?
nodes.body: Three triggers: (1) a payment made to the entity during the income year (s 109C); (2) a loan made to the entity during the income year (s 109D); or (3) all or part of a debt owed to the company is forgiven (s 109F). Each triggers a deemed dividend only if the shareholder/associate nexus is satisfied and no Subdivision D exception applies.

nodes.label: Payment made to an entity during the income year (s 109C)
nodes.body: A private company is taken to pay a dividend to an entity at the end of the income year if the company pays an amount to the entity during the year and the entity is a shareholder or associate at the time of payment, or a reasonable person would conclude the payment is made because the entity has been such a shareholder or associate (s 109C(1)(a)-(b)). 'Payment' includes amounts paid on behalf or for the benefit of the entity, credits, and transfers of property (s 109C(3)). A loan is not a payment (s 109C(3A)). Payment includes provision of an asset for use (s 109CA). Some payments are excluded by Subdivision D (ss 109J-109NA).

nodes.label: Loan made to an entity during the income year (s 109D)
nodes.body: A private company is taken to pay a dividend to an entity at the end of the income year if: (a) the company makes a loan to the entity during the current year; (b) the loan is not fully repaid before the lodgment day for the current year; (c) Subdivision D does not prevent the deemed dividend; and (d) the entity is a shareholder or associate (s 109D(1)(a)-(d)). 'Loan' includes an advance of money, provision of credit or financial accommodation, a payment with an obligation to repay, and any transaction that in substance effects a loan (s 109D(3)). A payment converted to a loan before the lodgment day is treated as a loan (s 109D(4A)). Liquidator's loans made in winding-up are covered by s 109D(1A)-(2).

nodes.label: Debt owed to the private company is forgiven (s 109F)
nodes.body: A private company is taken to pay a dividend to an entity at the end of the income year if all or part of a debt the entity owed the company is forgiven in that year and either: (a) the amount is forgiven when the entity is a shareholder or associate; or (b) a reasonable person would conclude the amount is forgiven because the entity has been such a shareholder or associate (s 109F(1)(a)-(b)). The amount of the dividend equals the amount forgiven, subject to s 109Y (s 109F(2)).

nodes.label: Is the dealing through an interposed entity or guarantee arrangement? (Subdiv E)
nodes.body: Division 7A extends to arrangements involving interposed entities. If a private company makes a payment or loan to an interposed entity as part of an arrangement involving a payment or loan to a target shareholder/associate, the Division operates as if the company made the payment or loan directly to the target (s 109T). Similarly, if the company guarantees a loan made by another entity as part of such an arrangement (s 109U). If yes, treat the dealing as made directly to the target entity before applying Subdivision D exceptions.

nodes.label: Trust UPE limb: Has the trustee made a payment, loan or forgiven a debt to a shareholder of a private company with an unpaid present entitlement?
nodes.body: Subdivision EA (s 109XA) applies where a trustee makes a payment (or loan or debt forgiveness) to a shareholder or associate of a private company, and the payment discharges or reduces a present entitlement of the shareholder that is wholly or partly attributable to an unrealised gain. If triggered, s 109XB deems a dividend paid by the private company. This is the 'trust UPE' limb of Division 7A — a parallel trigger that should be assessed alongside the main triggers.

nodes.label: Is the entity a shareholder or an associate of a shareholder, or is the dealing because of that capacity?
nodes.body: The shareholder/associate nexus must be satisfied for all three triggers. For payments (s 109C(1)(a)-(b)) and loans (s 109D(1)(d)(i)-(ii)): the entity must be a shareholder or associate at the time, or a reasonable person would conclude the dealing is because the entity has been such a shareholder or associate. For forgiven debts (s 109F(1)(a)-(b)): same test. Section 109ZE provides interpretation rules about entities. Section 109ZE defines 'associate' by reference to s 109ZE read with the entity rules in s 960-100 of ITAA 1997.

nodes.label: Is the dealing a payment under s 109C(3) and does a carve-out apply?
nodes.body: Section 109C(3) defines 'payment' broadly: (a) a payment to, on behalf of, or for the benefit of the entity; (b) a credit to, on behalf of, or for the benefit of the entity; (c) a transfer of property to the entity. However, a loan is not a payment (s 109C(3A)). A payment converted to a loan before lodgment day is treated as a loan under s 109D(4A). The value of a payment by transfer of property is the arm's length amount less consideration given (s 109C(4)). Additionally, no dividend arises if the amount is paid to a CGT concession stakeholder under s 152-325(1) of ITAA 1997 (s 109C(1) note).

statute.title: Payments treated as dividends

nodes.label: Is the amount paid to a CGT concession stakeholder (s 152-325(11) ITAA 1997)?
nodes.body: Section 109C(1) does not give rise to a dividend if the amount is paid to a CGT concession stakeholder under subsection 152-325(1) of ITAA 1997 (see subsection 152-325(11)). If this exception applies, no deemed dividend arises under the payment trigger.

statute.title: CGT concession stakeholder

nodes.label: Loan path: Is the loan fully repaid before the lodgment day?
nodes.body: A loan is only treated as a dividend under s 109D(1) if it is not fully repaid before the lodgment day for the current year (s 109D(1)(b)). 'Lodgment day' is defined in s 109D(6) as the earlier of: (a) the due date for lodgment of the company's return of income; and (b) the date of lodgment of the company's return of income. For non-resident companies, see s 109BC. If fully repaid by that date, no deemed dividend arises under s 109D(1). Certain payments relating to loans are not taken into account for working out how much has been repaid (s 109R).

nodes.label: Loan fully repaid before lodgment day — no deemed dividend under s 109D(1)
nodes.body: If the loan is fully repaid before the lodgment day for the current year, s 109D(1) does not apply. However, certain repayments may be disregarded under s 109R. Also, if the loan was made in the course of winding-up and not repaid, s 109D(1A) may apply in the following year.

nodes.label: Was the payment converted to a loan before the lodgment day? (s 109D(4A))
nodes.body: If a private company makes a payment to an entity and the payment is converted to a loan before the end of the private company's lodgment day for the year of income, the events are treated as a loan made to the entity at the time of the original payment (s 109D(4A)). This reclassification changes the trigger outcome from the payment path to the loan path.

statute.title: Loans treated as dividends

nodes.label: Does s 109J apply? — Payment discharging a pecuniary obligation at arm's length
nodes.body: Section 109J: A payment that discharges a genuine pecuniary obligation of the private company to the entity at arm's length is not treated as a dividend. This is the first Subdivision D exception.

statute.title: Payments discharging pecuniary obligations not treated as dividends

nodes.label: Does s 109K apply? — Inter-company payment or loan
nodes.body: Section 109K: A payment or loan made by a private company to another company is not treated as a dividend, subject to certain conditions. This exception covers payments and loans between related companies.

statute.title: Inter-company payments and loans not treated as dividends

nodes.label: Does s 109L apply? — Amount already assessable or excluded
nodes.body: Section 109L: Certain payments and loans are not treated as dividends if the amount is already assessable income of the entity or is otherwise excluded from the operation of Division 7A.

statute.title: Certain payments and loans not treated as dividends

nodes.label: Does s 109M apply? — Loan in ordinary course of business on arm's length terms
nodes.body: Section 109M: A loan made in the ordinary course of business on arm's length terms is not treated as a dividend. This requires the loan to be on terms that would be agreed between independent parties dealing at arm's length.

statute.title: Loans made in the ordinary course of business on arm's length terms not treated as dividends

nodes.label: Does s 109N apply? — Loan meeting minimum interest rate and maximum term criteria with written agreement
nodes.body: Section 109N: A loan is not treated as a dividend if it meets the minimum interest rate and maximum term criteria set out in s 109N(2)-(3), and there is a written loan agreement complying with s 109N(4). The minimum yearly repayment is worked out under s 109N(5)-(6).

statute.title: Loans meeting criteria for minimum interest rate and maximum term not treated as dividends

nodes.label: Does s 109NA apply? — Certain liquidator's distributions and loans
nodes.body: Section 109NA: Certain distributions and loans made by a liquidator are not treated as dividends. This exception applies to loans made in the course of winding-up, but if the loan is not fully repaid by the end of the following year, s 109D(1A) may apply.

statute.title: Certain liquidator's distributions and loans not treated as dividends

nodes.label: Exception applies — no deemed dividend
nodes.body: If any Subdivision D exception applies, the payment or loan is not treated as a dividend under s 109C or s 109D. For loans made in winding-up (s 109NA), if the loan is not fully repaid by the end of the following year, it may be treated as a dividend under s 109D(1A).

statute.title: Certain liquidator's distributions and loans not treated as dividends

rulings.title: Deemed Dividend: liquidator's loan not treated as a dividend

nodes.label: Is the debt forgiven under the s 109F(3)-(8) rules?
nodes.body: Section 109F defines when a debt is forgiven for Div 7A purposes. Rules: (3) Debt is forgiven if it would be forgiven under ITAA 1997 ss 245-35/245-37; (4) Discharge of a debt by transfer of property is NOT forgiveness; (5) Debt-parking assignments to associates may be forgiveness; (6) Failure to insist on payment may be forgiveness; (7) Forgiveness of constituent loan debt is taken as forgiveness of amalgamated loan debt; (8) If same debt is forgiven at different times under different provisions, only the earliest forgiveness applies.

statute.title: Forgiven debts treated as dividends

nodes.label: Does s 109G prevent a dividend from arising?
nodes.body: Section 109G provides that no dividend arises for: (1) forgiveness of a debt owed by another company (but not as trustee); (2) forgiveness because the debtor becomes bankrupt or Part X of the Bankruptcy Act applies; (3) forgiveness of a loan debt if the loan already gives rise to a dividend under s 109D or s 109E. If any of these apply, the forgiven debt does not give rise to a deemed dividend.

statute.title: Debt forgiveness that does not give rise to a dividend

nodes.label: Calculate the deemed dividend amount
nodes.body: For payments (s 109C): the amount paid is the dividend, subject to s 109Y. For loans (s 109D(1AA)): the amount of the dividend is the amount of the loan that has not been repaid before the lodgment day, subject to s 109Y. For liquidator's loans (s 109D(2)): the amount not repaid at the end of the current year. For forgiven debts (s 109F): the amount forgiven is the dividend, subject to s 109Y. If the loan was made in a previous year and the minimum yearly repayment is not met, an amalgamated loan shortfall is treated as a dividend under s 109E.

nodes.label: Is there an amalgamated loan from a previous year with a shortfall in the minimum yearly repayment?
nodes.body: An amalgamated loan from an earlier year is treated as a dividend at the end of the current year if: (a) the amalgamated loan is not repaid at the end of the current year; and (b) the amount paid during the year falls short of the minimum yearly repayment worked out under s 109E(5). The shortfall amount is the deemed dividend, subject to s 109Y. This applies in addition to any current-year loan.

nodes.label: Cap the total deemed dividends to the distributable surplus (s 109Y)
nodes.body: If the sum of all dividends the company is taken to pay under Division 7A at the end of the income year would exceed the company's distributable surplus, each dividend is proportionally reduced (s 109Y(1)). The distributable surplus is calculated as: net assets + Division 7A amounts - non-commercial loans - paid-up share value - repayments of non-commercial loans (s 109Y(2)). This cap applies to ALL deemed dividends under the Division.

nodes.label: Apply franking and character consequences (ss 109Z-109ZB)
nodes.body: A deemed dividend under Division 7A is taken to be paid to the entity as a shareholder (s 109Z(a)) and out of the company's profits (s 109Z(b)). It is disregarded for withholding tax purposes (s 109ZA). The amount treated as a dividend is not a fringe benefit (s 109ZB). The dividend is unfrankable under s 202-45(g) of ITAA 1997 — it cannot be franked, except where s 109RB or s 109RC allows franking.

nodes.label: Commissioner's decision: disregard the Division, allow franking, or no decision? (s 109RB)
nodes.body: If Division 7A would operate to treat an amount as a dividend, the Commissioner may make a decision under s 109RB(2) to: (a) disregard the operation of the Division (in whole or part) — resulting in no deemed dividend; or (b) allow the dividend to be franked. This discretion applies where the Commissioner considers it fair and reasonable having regard to: the extent of the shareholder's interest, the quantum of the deemed dividend, any distributions made, and other relevant circumstances, and where the result arises because of an honest mistake or inadvertent omission (s 109RB(1)-(4)).

statute.title: Commissioner may disregard operation of Division or allow dividend to be franked

nodes.label: Is the deemed dividend because of a family law obligation? (s 109RC)
nodes.body: Section 109RC: If a dividend is taken to be paid under Division 7A because of a family law obligation, the unfrankability rule in s 202-45(g)(i) of ITAA 1997 does not apply. The dividend can be franked at the company's benchmark franking percentage for the franking period (s 109RC(1)-(3)). If not because of a family law obligation, the deemed dividend remains unfrankable.

statute.title: Dividend may be franked if taken to be paid because of family law obligation

nodes.label: Deemed dividend applies — assessable as a dividend
nodes.body: The amount is included in the shareholder's assessable income as a dividend under s 44(1) of ITAA 1936, capped at the distributable surplus. The dividend is unfrankable unless s 109RB (Commissioner discretion) or s 109RC (family law obligation) permits franking. The private company must account for franking debits. Review options: the Commissioner may exercise discretion under s 109RB or the taxpayer may object under Part IVC.

nodes.label: No deemed dividend under Division 7A
nodes.body: The dealing does not give rise to a deemed dividend under Division 7A. This may be because: the entity was not a shareholder or associate, the loan was fully repaid before lodgment day, a Subdivision D exception applied, the distributable surplus was nil, the Commissioner exercised discretion under s 109RB to disregard the operation, or the s 109G debt forgiveness exception applied. The dealing is assessed under ordinary principles if applicable.

nodes.label: No Division 7A trigger — dealing outside scope
nodes.body: The dealing does not fall within any of the three triggers (payment, loan, forgiven debt) or the shareholder/associate nexus is not satisfied. No deemed dividend arises under Division 7A. The transaction may still be assessed under other provisions of the income tax law.
